item.title: Looking for someone to rewrite The Kephart Arc: Looking for someone to rewrite The Kephart Arc
item.content:encoded:
Hi everyone!

So, back during JamCon One, I wrote one segment of the same story for each prompt, each an SCP focusing on a pair of researchers investigating a creepy company. They are sequential on the mainlist, SCP-3643, SCP-3644, and SCP-3645. I reread them recently and I think they're some of my worst work, because I was attempting to write in a way I normally don't, but they also don't deserve to be deleted. I won't delete them if anyone wants to take a crack at rewriting them and trying to fix some of their flaws. Does anyone want to try?

item.title: SCP Reference Help: Re: SCP Reference Help
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the response! Right yeah, exactly. The events that occur are more important than the things that they occur upon. But if you'll pardon the metaphor: That's why I'm trying to find a heading to set sail. Because I wish to find uncharted waters, but I can't do that if I don't know what's ahead of me. That is to say, I don't wish to come anywhere near those other two magnifying glass SCPs.

You mention that "my ideas are fine for that reason". I hope what that means is that this is somewhat true, my "jumping off" concept is original enough to weave it's own tale. But I will take that with a grain of salt. If you mention there are two others, I would like to know them, to avoid those "waters"; this was the intent in my question. I will have to go through an arduous process to spin a story that's foundation worthy, but I don't want to tread any lines already made. Sincerely, I thank you again.

item.title: SCP Reference Help: Re: SCP Reference Help
item.content:encoded:
I think you should be less concerned with the basic anomalous properties of your object and more with the story that it's couched in. It doesn't particularly matter if we have two magnifying glass SCPs if they tell different stories. Your ideas are fine for that reason.

I mean, I'm not particularly speaking to the cohesion of the ideas themselves — the invulnerable man trope doesn't particularly interest me and a magnifying glass that sees things really good seems pretty straightforward. Just a fair warning, although all this should be ironed out in the idea crit process.

item.title: SCP Reference Help: SCP Reference Help
item.content:encoded:
I've seen a number of SCPs myself, but not enough. So at the moment there are 2 ideas that might have some potential.

1) An object that can observe past histories

2) A D-class that does not die

.

+ show block
– hide block

With the first, I originally concepted this object being a magnifying glass, however I did note after conception that there's a magnifying glass entry on some knock-off SCP website that refers to themselves as scp classic? Store, cache, preserve? Even if it isn't canon I think my concept can be mixed up a bit more than taking that specific form.

The key element is that this object would be able to reference an edit log for anything that is seen through it. You know, how on some of these posts you can see an edit history? That's the idea, but it could be all contents ever written on a whiteboard. Or in a notebook. But even deeper, say in a long held manuscript; like the Quran, or the Bible. Maybe even ████████ material? Naturally the key to this concept would be in the story surrounding it, but I want to know if this idea exists in the scp lore in anyway. I'm sure people have used time travel in their creation, but this specific trait just might be limiting enough to push a tale.

I do comprehend, being able to see redacted material is a dangerous idea, being that author makes that information unavailable to guide the mystery of it. But if used correctly, it has good potential to revive an old topic. Obviously requires a test of scrutiny.

.

The second concept is a lesser one in which I simply considered: What if there was a D-class that always survived their testing? If we apply this nature to a soldier or a doctor? Sure, there is some possibility, but D-class always gets the worst of it. So again, I want to know if there's any D-class that are SCPs.

This idea has less wiggle room being, at the moment, it's just an entity with writers shield. But there might be some fun to be had with this concept. P.S. I am not thinking of a character trait like Marvel's Darwin, where his body just adapts to any situation. Not my intent what-so-ever. Nor do I wish to pursue some "he's just lucky" trait akin to Domino. What would the D-class be I dunno, but I don't want to start concepting if there's already another similar D-class on the list.

.

If you can help I'd dearly appreciate it.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: How to write something in a canon when no one else has heard it before?: How to write something in a canon when no one else has heard it before?
item.content:encoded:
I was seeking feedback as well as greenlight for a concept of a tale, and it takes place in the Apotheosis Canon during the 2018 Doomsday Challenge. I assumed a good chunk of members here in the wiki read or at least heard of this canon.

I PM'd a critter and they told me that they weren't familiar with the canon, nor are they interested in reading the canon to provide further critique. As well with other criticism they were able to provide. I told them that I understood and wished them a nice day.

Today I edited my concept around the criticisms I did got and went out seeking feedback again.

So how do I write for a canon that possibly no one else is aware of?

item.title: Help with posting a comment: Re: Help with posting a comment
item.content:encoded:
Where may I post a question regarding the use of Foundation personnel like Dr. Bright and Dr. Clef?

If it's about the characters of Bright or Clef, like the lore surrounding them, then you should post in the Foundation Universe forum (or ask around on IRC or Discord). If you've got a writing-related question, like if you are able to use them, then the Questions Desk is the right spot.

May I use a character I wrote myself, or do I need to borrow an existing character?

You can do whichever! Throwaway doctors are very normal and nearly expected, since the inclusion of Bright or Clef or any other major character carries a bit of baggage with them — you know, why is Bright/Clef in this story? Why would they be interviewing this anomaly? When in doubt, just use an original character.

item.title: Can I Get Draft Critique on a Mainlist Rewrite?: Re: Can I Get Draft Critique on a Mainlist Rewrite?
item.content:encoded: Indeed, yes. You have a successful article on the site, so you've exempted yourself from the greenlighting process as long as it, or another successful article, stays up.

item.title: Sandbox format question: Re: Sandbox format question
item.content:encoded:
The sandbox you linked is using the Black Highlighter CSS Theme.

More info: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/theme:black-highlighter-theme

Basically, at the top of your page copy and paste: [[include :scp-wiki:theme:black-highlighter-theme]]

If you want the dark sidebar, copy and paste this underneath: [[include :scp-wiki:component:bhl-dark-sidebar]]

item.title: Can I Get Draft Critique on a Mainlist Rewrite?: Can I Get Draft Critique on a Mainlist Rewrite?
item.content:encoded:
Little bit unorthodox, I suppose. I understand that first time authors need two greenlights before posting in the Draft Critique Forum, but the FAQ states that if you have a "successful" (meaning voted positively, I guess?) main list article you can bypass the greenlight process, and go straight to Draft Critique.

So, hypothetically, let's say I wasn't completely happy with an article I posted, and thought about doing a bit of a rewrite; could I post the rewritten draft in the Draft Critique Forum without greenlights, on the basis that the original article is currently positively rated on the main site?
